tagline: First close-up images of a cometary nucleus — flew 596 km past Halley's Comet at 68 km/s in 1986
description: ESA's first deep-space probe. Spin-stabilised drum-shaped bus protected by a Whipple-shield dust bumper, built around the Halley Multicolour Camera plus 9 other instruments contributed by 11 European countries, NASA, and Japan. Closest approach to comet 1P/Halley on 1986-03-14 at 596 km — the bumper survived, though a 100 mg dust strike 14 seconds before closest approach offset the spin axis and broke camera contact. Reactivated in 1990 for a 200 km flyby of comet Grigg-Skjellerup in 1992, the first time a spacecraft returned to a different cometary target.
best_known_for: First close-up images of a cometary nucleus — 596 km past Halley's Comet, 1986-03-14
